div.head: AGu Prol.
div.ab: Ðis is ðæt frið, ðæt Ælfred cyninc ⁊ Gyðrum cyning ⁊ ealles Angelcynnes witan ⁊ eal seo ðeod ðe on Eastænglum beoð ealle gecweden habbað ⁊ mid aðum gefeostnod for hy sylfe ⁊ for heora gingran, ge for geborene ge for ungeborene, ðe Godes miltse recce oððe ure.
Ðis is þæt frið, ðæt Ælfred cyng ⁊ Guðrum cing ⁊ ealles Angelcynnes witan ⁊ eal seo ðeod ðe on Eastenglum beoð, ⁊ gesworen habbað, ge for hy sylfe ge for heora ofspryng.

Hęc sunt pacis agenda, que Ælfredus rex et Godrun rex et omnes Anglie sapientes et omnis populus, qui in Eastanglia manet, constituerunt et iureiurando confirmauerunt pro se ipsis et iunioribus suis, progenitis et ingenitis, qui Dei misericordiam diligunt et nostram.

Ðis is ðæt frið, ðæt Ælfred cyninc ⁊ Gyðrum cyning ⁊ ealles Angelcynnes witan ⁊ eal seo ðeod ðe on Eastænglum beoð ealle gecweden habbað ⁊ mid aðum gefeostnod for hy sylfe ⁊ for heora gingran, ge for geborene ge for ungeborene, ðe Godes miltse reccen oððe ure.

Dies ist der Friede, welchen König Aelfred und König Guthrum und die Witan der ganzen Englischen Nation und das ganze Volk, welches in Ostanglien ist, alle bestimmt und mit Eiden gefestigt (beschworen B2) haben für sich selbst und für ihre Nachkommen (Nachkommenschaft B2), so für geborene wie für noch nicht-geborene, die Gottes Gnade erstreben oder die unsere.

This is the peace which King Alfred and King Guthrum and the councillors of the whole English nation and all the people who are in East Anglia have all determined and confirmed with oaths (sworn B2), for themselves and for their descendants (offspring B2), both born and not yet born, who seek God’s mercy or ours.

These are the terms of peace which King Alfred and King Guthrum, and the councillors of all the English nation, and all the people who dwell in East Anglia, have all agreed upon and confirmed with oaths, on their own behalf and for their subjects, both living and unborn, who are anxious for God's favour and ours.

This is the peace which King Alfred and King Guthrum and the councillors of all the English race and all the people which is in East Anglia have all agreed on and confirmed with oaths, for themselves and for their subjects, both for the living and those yet unborn, who care to have God’s grace or ours.

Auf Ælfred folgt Guthrum, offenbar nur weil dieser König dem Adel vorangehen soll; s. o. Einl. 4
Guthrum follows Ælfred, evidently only because this king is meant to precede the nobility; see above Introduction 4

Nicht ‘Angelvolk’, was als Ggs. zu Sachsen oder zu allen Dänen missdeutbar wäre; s. o. Einl. 4. König und Witan (s. d. Gl 2. 3a. 8) vertreten den Englischen Staat; ein neben der Krone gleichberechtigtes ‘Volk’ darf man in letzteren nicht sehen

Not ‘Angle people’, which could be misinterpreted as a contrast to Saxons or to all Danes; see above Introduction 4. King and witan (see that word in Gl 2. 3a. 8) represent the English state; one must not see in the latter a ‘people’ with rights equal to those of the crown

Mitzuverstehen neben eigentlichem Ostanglien ist Essex und ein südöstlicher Teil Merciens. Und zwar sicher nicht Dänen allein, sondern auch freie Untertanen Guthrums von Englischer Abkunft. Die Münzen schlugen für ihn Angelsachsen und Franken; Keary Catal. of Ags. coins 95ff.

Besides East Anglia proper, Essex and a south-eastern part of Mercia are to be understood as included. And certainly not Danes alone, but also free subjects of Guthrum of English descent. His coins were struck for him by Anglo-Saxons and Franks; Keary Catal. of Ags. coins 95ff.
S. o. Einl. 4
See above Introduction 4
Die Lesart B's, von B2 nur verwässert, wird bestätigt durch die Formel, die der Agsä. Annalist zu den Verträgen Eadweards I. und Æthelstans mit den Nordleuten 921. 926 braucht: þæt fæstnodon mid aðum

B's reading, merely watered down by B2, is confirmed by the formula which the Anglo-Saxon annalist uses for the treaties of Eadweard I and Æthelstan with the Northmen in 921. 926: þæt fæstnodon mid aðum
sich, die Untergebenen und die Nachkommen bindend
binding themselves, their subordinates and their descendants

bessere meine Übs : ‘Untergebene [bes. Unterbeamte]’, laut Wb. und II Em Pro. Unter iuniores meint Q diesen Sinn. — Dagegen zog B2 das Satzende kürzend zusammen. Vielleicht brachte ihn ungeborene (s. d. Wb) auf ‘Nachkommenschaft’, da es in einer Urkundenformel hinter ofspring erscheint. Oder aber schon er missverstand gingran, wie das Mittelengl. vorkommt: in Ælfreds Testament (Bi 553f.) werden des Königs Worte mine mægcild oððe yldran oððe gingran später modernisiert durch olde or yonge. — Meine frühere Übersetzung folgte der bisher üblichen, die Earle Anglo-S. liter. 157 zuletzt vertrat. Eindeutig heisst gingran ‘Kinder’ im Ggs. zu Eltern bei Hom. n. Wulfstan ed. Napier p. 38 = 301

Correct my transl. to ‘subordinates [esp. subordinate officials]’, according to Wb and II Em Pro. By iuniores Q means this sense. — B2, on the other hand, contracted and shortened the end of the sentence. Perhaps ungeborene (see that word in Wb) led him to ‘offspring’, since it appears after ofspring in a charter formula. Or else he himself already misunderstood gingran, as occurs in Middle English: in Ælfred's will (Bi 553f.) the king's words mine mægcild oððe yldran oððe gingran are later modernised as olde or yonge. — My earlier translation followed the one hitherto usual, last advocated by Earle Anglo-S. liter. 157. gingran unambiguously means ‘children’, in contrast to parents, in Hom. n. Wulfstan ed. Napier p. 38 = 301

note.label: reccen
note.seg: recce. MSS.

This interesting document, which, since London is left on the English side of the boundary, was probably drawn up after Alfred obtained London in 886, survives in two versions, both in C.C.C.C., MS. 383. I give the longer of the two versions, which also occurs in the Latin of Quadripartitus. The code is certainly no later than 890, for in this year Guthrum died. The text is edited by Liebermann, I, 126–9; and with English translation by Attenborough, pp. 98–101, Thorpe, I, 152–7
